newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says French aid to Kimberly-Clark was illegal.
newsitem.headline: Court says French aid to Kimberly-Clark was illegal.

text.p: The European Court of Justice dismissed on Thursday a bid by the French Republic to annul the Commission's classification as state aid of funds from a French National Employment Fund (FNE) to Kimberly Clark Sopalin.
In 1993, Kimberly Clark, under a company reconstruction plan, dismissed employees under a social plan governed by French law. Twenty-five percent, FF 27.25 million, of that plan was funded by France.

The Commission declared France's contribution to Kimberly Clark's social plan as illegal state aid under EC Treaty article 92, saying it was intended to facilitate the development of certain economic activities.
The Commission attatched importance to the reduction of capacity at Kimberly Clark, that the laid-off workers were the main beneficiaries and the limited amount of aid granted.
France claimed the Commission errred in law as the mechanism put into place by the FNE constitutes a general measure for the benefit of employees intended to combat unemployment.
But the court found the treaty does not distinguish between measures of state intervention based on their causes or aims, but defines them in relation to their effects.
"The social character of the FNE assistance is not therefore sufficient to exclude it outright from being catergorized as aid," the court said.

The court found that under the system FNE operates, contributions to certain undertakings may place them in a more favourable situation than their competitors, classifying such contributions as state aid.
(Court transltion into English. Original language of the case: French)
"Concept of state aid within the meaning of article 92(1) of the Treaty - State intervention of a social character"
Commission of the European Communities, defendant
application for annulment of Commission decision SG(94)D/8907 of 27 June 1994 concerning aid to the company Kimberly Clark Sopalin
